title: fix(app-shell): name a `labelling: control` widget from its grid column header (#9889)
body:
Fixes #9889

⚠️ **Angle-bracket notation is deliberately spelled out in words** throughout this body (LABEL element, TH cell, TD cell). GitHub's body sanitizer deletes tag-shaped fragments on save — backticks and fenced blocks do not protect them — and half of this text is about markup.

---

## ⭐ First deliverable — the question, answered from the registry

> **Is `labelling` a two-valued distinction that should be collapsed, or does `'control'` mean something the naming channel genuinely cannot serve?**

**Neither. It stays two-valued, and `'control'` names nothing the IDREF cannot serve.** The reading, from `WIDGET_LABELLING` and its two prose sections:

`labelling` answers **exactly one** question — *can the host's LABEL element with `for` reach a labelable element?* `'control'` says yes (the widget puts the host `id` on the one labelable element that is the field's primary control); `'group'` says no (the field IS a container — `for` is inert on it). That single answer is what `FieldRow` branches on: `htmlFor` + `id` down, versus an `id` published on the LABEL and handed down as `ariaLabelledBy`. It is a real structural fact about the DOM each widget renders, and collapsing it re-opens the dangling `for` that objectui#3978 and objectui#4010 ruled against — or strips click-to-focus from eleven real controls. ⛔ Do not collapse it.

What was wrong is a **second** meaning read into it: that `'control'` also declares *which naming channel the widget consumes*. It never did. `FieldRow`'s "exactly one of `id` / `ariaLabelledBy`" is a rule about **a host that has a LABEL**. A grid/table repeater cell has none (objectui#5063), names each cell from its TH column header by IDREF, keeps the cell id on the control as a plain anchor — and therefore hands down **both**. `FieldControl`'s own prop doc already says this in as many words, and its builtin branches already emit both. Only the twenty registry widgets were left behind, and the nine `'group'` ones happened to be right by accident of which prop they read.

⚠️ **The caution in the dispatch did not survive the reading, and I checked it specifically.** "Some `'control'` widgets genuinely cannot take an IDREF (a composite that renders several inputs, say)" — none of the eleven is such a composite. Each renders exactly one primary labelable element per arm, plus auxiliary affordances that already carry their own names, which is verbatim what the `'control'` contract says. `aria-labelledby` is valid on a labelable element, so the same element takes both. ⇒ "make them all consume it" **is** the right shape here.

⇒ The repair is not a collapse and not a widening of `labelling`. It is one file-local `controlNaming({ id, ariaLabelledBy })` helper that every `'control'` widget spreads onto its primary control, in every arm.

## ⭐ Re-derived: the bound that justified letting this grow — **it has NOT moved**

objectui#9859 enlarged this population and was accepted because no shipped metadata declares a grid repeater. Re-derived here, at objectstack `ed6c554545c01960579da643930e5177731d58a0`, 2026-09-18T17:13Z, one command:

| reading | result |
|:--|:--|
| TARGET — a field spec declaring `widget: 'grid'` **or** `widget: 'table'`, shipped `.form.ts` / object / plugin sources, tests excluded | **0 lines** |
| MATCHER control, same regex, same run — three known spellings in a fixture | **3 of 3 fire** |
| CORPUS control — live repeater field specs in the same corpus, same command | **25 lines**, printed |
| CORPUS control — field specs carrying any widget | **73 lines**, printed |

⭐ Two corrections to the dispatch's framing, both in the direction of *more* confidence, not less:

1. The bound was stated as `widget: 'grid'`. `RepeaterField` actually takes the grid layout on **`widget === 'grid' || widget === 'table'`**, so the instrument that justified the trade was narrower than the trigger. **Re-derived on the wider one, the zero still holds.** (objectui#9859's own changeset already used the wider spelling — the dispatch gloss did not.)
2. The counts differ from the relayed 21 / 51 because my corpus is stated rather than inherited: shipped sources in the sibling `objectstack` checkout, tests excluded. Same subject, same command, controls firing.

⚠️ **Radius of that zero:** it covers metadata **shipped in the two repositories**. It says nothing about metadata an installation authors at runtime, which is the whole point of a metadata-driven designer — so "latent" means "not shipped", ⛔ not "unreachable".

## ⭐ How my census probe sees through a spread

The dispatch warns that a first probe matched the literal attribute `aria-labelledby={ariaLabelledBy}` and missed a widget reaching the channel through a spread. Mine keys on the **identifier reaching the component body**, not on the attribute spelling: it slices each registered component's body by brace-matching from its declaration, then tests the body for the `ariaLabelledBy` identifier (which catches destructuring, rename, `props.ariaLabelledBy`, and building it into an object that is later spread), and reports the literal-attribute answer as a **second column** so the two can be compared rather than conflated.

**It reproduces the difference in-band.** On `origin/main` `fc12bc8c6`:

```
color-picker      group    ident=YES  literalAttr=no   <-- reaches the channel ONLY through a spread
---
control: 0/11 reach ariaLabelledBy
group:   9/9 reach ariaLabelledBy
```

`ColorSwatchGroupWidget` builds `{ ariaLabelledBy }` into a `naming` object and spreads it — a literal probe scores `'group'` at 8/9 and reports a widget as broken that is not. ⭐ And after this change the point sharpens: **all eleven** repaired widgets read `ident=YES literalAttr=no`, so a literal probe would now report `0/11` repaired. The blind spot the probe still has is a component that spreads all of its props without ever naming this one; the probe reports that case as a labelled blind spot and found none.

## What changed

`packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/widgets.tsx` only — ⛔ no `SchemaForm.tsx` edit is needed, because `FieldControl` already hands both channels to a registered widget.

- one file-local `controlNaming({ id, ariaLabelledBy })`, spread at **21 sites** across the eleven `'control'` widgets, replacing a bare `id={id}`, in every arm each can render;
- `filter-builder` forwards the IDREF one level into `FilterBuilderField`, whose other call site (inside `FilterModeWidget`'s tab editor) is a sub-control of a group and deliberately gets neither channel;
- `color-input` and `secret` carry an `aria-label` fallback for a caller with no host label; it was suppressed on `id` alone and is now suppressed on **either** channel, so the fallback cannot sit beside a live IDREF (the one-label-one-channel rule of objectui#3978);
- three doc blocks corrected where they stated the defect as the contract: `WidgetProps.ariaLabelledBy` ("`undefined` for `'control'` widgets"), `WidgetProps.id` (a `'group'` widget does receive a cell id in the grid path, as a plain anchor), and the `'control'` section of `WIDGET_LABELLING`, which now states the exemption explicitly.

Every edit was applied by a script that **asserts each anchor matches exactly once** and refuses otherwise — a zero-hit replacement exits non-zero rather than silently doing nothing.

## What is pinned — both sides and the negative

`packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/SchemaForm.controlWidgetGridNaming-9889.test.tsx`, 38 assertions, **all from a real `SchemaForm` render reading the computed accessible name** — ⛔ never a source-text or prop assertion.

1. each of the eleven `'control'` widgets, driven into a grid cell, has `toHaveAccessibleName` equal to its column, *and* its IDREF is shown to land on an element whose tag is TH;
2. the case list is checked **against `WIDGET_LABELLING` itself**, so a twelfth `'control'` widget cannot be added without a reading here;
3. both channels land on the **same** element — the named control is the one carrying the cell id;
4. **the same-render control:** `condition` and `multiselect` (`'group'`) still answer that same IDREF. If the change had *moved* the channel rather than widened it, these go red;
5. **the untouched channel:** all eleven in the card layout are still named by a LABEL element with `for`, and carry **no** `aria-labelledby`;
6. ⭐ **the negative:** the reveal toggle inside `secret` and the hex mirror inside `color-input` keep their own names, carry no IDREF, and are not renamed after the column.

⚠️ The negative exists because the plausible "completion" of this change is to spread the naming over a widget's whole subtree, which turns a grid row into controls that all announce the same thing. That is now a red test, not a comment.

## Ablation — a value the two implementations disagree about

Run at this branch's head, mutation proved by **blob hash**, restore proved by hash equality **and** an empty `git diff HEAD`, trap on EXIT/INT/TERM with absolute paths. Anchors are asserted to match exactly once, so a no-op mutation fails loudly.

⭐ **The value chosen is the IDREF in a grid cell.** In the **card** layout old and new produce byte-identical DOM (the host sends no IDREF there), so an ablation measured on a card row comes back green against both implementations and proves nothing. The signature below is what makes the pin discriminating rather than merely red:

| leg | mutation | result |
|:--|:--|:--|
| fix | none | `38 passed` |
| **A** | `controlNaming` returns the id alone — exactly the pre-change behaviour | `13 failed / 25 passed` — **all 11** `'control'` grid cases + both negatives red; ⭐ **both `'group'` cases and all 11 card-layout cases stay GREEN** |
| **B** | spread `controlNaming` onto `secret`'s reveal toggle — the wrong "completion" | `1 failed / 37 passed` — **only** the exemption pin |
| restore | none | `38 passed`, hash back to base |

No build step is involved: these tests import the module through a relative source specifier, so there is no `dist` between the mutation and the assertion.

## Verification

| command | verdict |
|:--|:--|
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/ packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/column-identity.ratchet.test.ts` | `Test Files 725 passed (725)` · `Tests 7163 passed | 1 skipped (7164)` — `VERDICT command-exit 0` |
| `pnpm exec vitest run apps/console/` | `Test Files 101 passed (101)` · `Tests 1158 passed (1158)` — `VERDICT command-exit 0` |
| `packages/app-shell` → `tsc --noEmit` then `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` (the full `type-check` script) | `0 errors`, exit 0 — ⚠️ only after `turbo run build --filter=@object-ui/app-shell^...`; a fresh worktree gives 670 TS2307 from unbuilt dependencies, a prerequisite and ⛔ not a red gate |
| `packages/app-shell` → `eslint .` | `0 errors, 3041 warnings` — the repo-wide warning baseline; `--max-warnings` is deliberately unset here. ⛔ My diff adds and removes **no** export site, so the `react-refresh` subject set is unchanged (the helper is file-local for exactly this reason) |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | exit 0 — one changeset declared for one published source file |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` | exit 0 |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-claims.mjs` | exit 0 (report-only) |
| `node scripts/check-pending-changeset-literals.mjs` | exit 0 |
| `node scripts/check-control-bytes.mjs` | exit 0, 8000 files; plus a direct control-byte grep over my three files — no hits |
| `node scripts/check-new-cross-file-line-citations.mjs` | `0 new citation(s)`, exit 0 |
| `node scripts/check-test-path-roots.mjs` | exit 0 |
| `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` (my three paths) | `NOT GOVERNED` — the ordinary route |

Every heavy run went through `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh` in the sibling checkout; each verdict above is that script's `VERDICT` line, ⛔ not a bare exit status.

**The sweep.** Tests naming the changed module were enumerated **by concept, not by identifier** — the labelling channel, the grid-cell naming channel, the registry table, accessible-name assertions — with a deliberately-absent token as the same-run control (zero hits, so the enumerator is not matching every file). It returns 20 files that reach the module and 19 that name the concept, two of them **outside** `packages/app-shell` (`packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/column-identity.ratchet.test.ts` and `packages/app-shell/src/views/view-filter-fold.ratchet.test.ts`). Since the package barrel re-exports this family and `apps/console` consumes it through the src alias, a narrowing below the package is not provable ⇒ the whole package ran, plus that out-of-package ratchet test by path. ⭐ **And `apps/console` ran too**: the same concept-level enumeration finds 8 console tests reaching this family, so stopping at the package boundary would have been the same unprovable narrowing one level up.

⚠️ **One verdict was discarded rather than reported.** An earlier invocation joined the console run and a throwaway probe with `;`, and the wrapper printed `VERDICT batch-last-exit 0 — NOT A VERDICT ON THE WHOLE COMMAND`. That is not a reading, so the console suite was re-run as a command of its own for the verdict quoted above.

**Pending-changeset sweep.** 14 pending `.changeset/` bodies mention this subject; each was read. ⛔ None is made false by this diff. The nearest, `9859-repeater-grid-widget-detectors.md`, states the cell "names each cell from its column header by IDREF" — still true, and now true for every widget rather than nine of twenty. `select-empty-host-id-8803.md`, `3991-builtin-select-empty-state-label-for.md` and `record-picker-label-association-5771.md` are all about `@object-ui/components` / `@object-ui/fields` registrations, a different registry. ⛔ No other card's changeset was edited.

## Adjacency — re-derived, ⛔ not taken from the dispatch

PR objectui#9923 (card objectui#9912), read from its **file list** via the REST API at 2026-09-18T17:13Z, ⛔ not from its title and ⛔ not from its branch name:

```
added     .changeset/9912-schemaform-ref-indirection.md
added     packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/SchemaForm.refIndirection-9912.test.tsx
modified  packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/SchemaForm.tsx
```

Three files, `state: open`, `mergeable_state: behind`. **Zero overlap** with this branch's three paths — same directory, disjoint files. ⇒ no serialization owed, and this branch deliberately does not touch `SchemaForm.tsx` even for the stale comment noted below, so the near miss stays a miss.

## Acceptance notes — out of scope, ⛔ not fixed here

- **To file (measured, with dedupe words).** `'control'` widgets whose catalog-failure arm renders **no labelable element at all**: `PickerLoadFailure` replaces the picker, so the host id lands nowhere and `FieldRow`'s LABEL element with `for` dangles. Measured in a card-layout render, each widget's failure arm and loaded arm read in the **same test**, so the loaded arm is the control:

  ```
  field-ref         ERROR-ARM for=mdf-probe hostIdEl=NONE   ||  LOADED-ARM for=mdf-probe hostIdEl=BUTTON
  view-ref          ERROR-ARM for=mdf-probe hostIdEl=NONE   ||  LOADED-ARM for=mdf-probe hostIdEl=BUTTON
  object-selector   ERROR-ARM for=mdf-probe hostIdEl=NONE   ||  LOADED-ARM for=mdf-probe hostIdEl=BUTTON
  field-selector    ERROR-ARM for=mdf-probe hostIdEl=INPUT  ||  LOADED-ARM for=mdf-probe hostIdEl=INPUT
  ```

  ⚠️ **`field-selector` is NOT MEASURED, ⛔ not negative.** It loads its catalog through its own fetch rather than through `widgetContext.objectFields`, so this probe never put it in its failure arm — it landed on the no-object-bound arm, which is healthy. By source reading it has the same shape, but that is a hypothesis here, not a reading. Three widgets are measured DANGLING. The `'control'` contract in `WIDGET_LABELLING` says verbatim: *"The widget puts `id` on the ONE labelable element that is the field's primary control, in EVERY branch it can render"* — the failure arm was added after that sentence and is not covered by it. Same class as objectui#4871 / objectui#4788, and the same shape objectui#8803 repaired for `field:select` by making its empty state an OUTPUT element. Unrelated to this card: in a grid cell that arm renders no control, so it is ⛔ not the unnamed-edit-box defect. Dedupe words: `PickerLoadFailure arm has no labelable element` · `control widget failure arm dangling label for` · `object-selector load failure unnamed` · `labelling control contract EVERY branch` · `field-ref error arm no host id`.
- **Noted, not filed.** `FieldControl` carries a comment above its registered-widget render reading "Exactly one of these is defined, decided by the widget's own `labelling` declaration" — false for the grid-cell path, and contradicted by that same component's own `ariaLabelledBy` prop doc a few dozen lines above it. It is documentation drift, ⛔ not a runtime defect, and it lives in `SchemaForm.tsx`, which PR objectui#9923 is live in. Successor who will touch that file: objectui#9923's author, or the next `SchemaForm` card. ⛔ Not repaired here, to keep the directory-level near miss a miss.

## Landing

⛔ Draft on purpose. ⛔ Not marked ready, ⛔ no auto-merge, ⛔ not merged. No label was applied: the changeset declaration is this repository's real mechanism and `skip-changeset` is inert here, so a label write would be theatre.

⛔ No `Clause-②:` line is copied from the claim comment because the claim carries none — this repository's `Check Changeset` reads the declared changeset, which is present.
